newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Institutional Investor raises Israel's ranking.
newsitem.headline: Institutional Investor raises Israel's ranking.

text.p: The U.S. magazine Institutional Investor has raised Israel's ranking to 40 from 41, indicating the country is a lower risk, the Treasury said in a statement.
The ranking is based on six-month data until September.
Out of the 14 countries in the Middle East Israel was rated seven, up from eight.
Institutional Investor ranks countries on various criteria including economic indicators, access to financial markets, sovereign credit rating and political risk.
In the areas of short-term credit access, access to credit from international banks and ability to repay debt, Israel received the maximum marks, the Treasury said.
Last week the magazine Euromoney also raised Israel's ranking to 32 from 33.
